questions.prompt: What is the relative charge of a proton?
questions.explanation: Protons have a relative charge of +1, electrons −1 and neutrons 0.

questions.prompt: Which particle has a very small relative mass and a charge of −1?
questions.explanation: Electrons have a relative charge of −1 and a tiny mass compared with protons and neutrons.

questions.prompt: Match each particle to its relative charge and mass.
questions.explanation: Protons and neutrons both have a relative mass of 1; electrons are much lighter.

questions.prompt: The number of protons in an atom is called its ___ number.
questions.explanation: The atomic number is the number of protons. All atoms of an element have the same number of protons.

questions.prompt: A sodium atom has atomic number 11 and mass number 23. How many neutrons does it have?
questions.explanation: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 23 − 11 = 12.

questions.prompt: Why do atoms have no overall electrical charge?
questions.correct: They have equal numbers of protons and electrons
wrong: They have equal numbers of protons and neutrons
questions.explanation: Each proton (+1) is balanced by an electron (−1), so the charges cancel out.

questions.prompt: Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons are called ___.
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same number of protons but a different number of neutrons, so a different mass number.

questions.prompt: What is the electronic structure of sodium (atomic number 11)?
questions.explanation: The first shell holds 2 electrons and the second holds 8, leaving 1 in the third shell: 2,8,1.

questions.prompt: Put these models of the atom in the order they were developed, earliest first.
items: Atoms are tiny spheres that can't be divided
Plum pudding: a ball of positive charge with electrons in it
Nuclear model: the mass is in a tiny positive nucleus
Bohr: electrons orbit the nucleus at set distances
Chadwick shows there are neutrons in the nucleus
questions.explanation: Solid spheres → plum pudding (after electrons were discovered) → nuclear model (alpha scattering) → Bohr's shells → neutrons.

questions.prompt: In the alpha particle scattering experiment, most alpha particles went straight through the gold foil. What did this show?
questions.correct: Most of the atom is empty space
wrong: The atom is a solid sphere
questions.explanation: Most particles passed straight through, so most of the atom must be empty space, with mass in a tiny nucleus.

questions.prompt: Why do elements in the same group of the periodic table react in similar ways?
questions.correct: They have the same number of electrons in their outer shell
wrong: They have the same mass number
They have the same number of neutrons
They have the same number of shells
questions.explanation: Chemical properties depend on the outer electrons, and elements in a group have the same number of them.

questions.prompt: Why are the noble gases (Group 0) unreactive?
questions.correct: They have a stable arrangement of electrons (a full outer shell)
questions.explanation: Noble gases have full outer shells, a stable arrangement, so they don't easily gain, lose or share electrons.

questions.prompt: How does the reactivity of the Group 1 metals change going down the group?
questions.explanation: Going down Group 1, the outer electron is further from the nucleus, so it's lost more easily and reactivity increases.

questions.prompt: Group 1 metals react with water to make a metal hydroxide and ___ gas.
questions.explanation: For example, sodium + water → sodium hydroxide + hydrogen.

questions.prompt: Why do the Group 7 elements get less reactive going down the group?
questions.correct: The outer shell is further from the nucleus, so it's harder to gain an electron
wrong: They have more electrons to lose
questions.explanation: Halogens react by gaining an electron. Further down, the outer shell is further from the nucleus, so this is harder.

questions.prompt: Chlorine water is added to potassium bromide solution. What happens?
questions.correct: Chlorine displaces bromine and the solution turns orange
wrong: Nothing, because bromine is more reactive
questions.explanation: Chlorine is more reactive than bromine, so it displaces it from its salt; the bromine colours the solution orange.

questions.prompt: Match each separation method to what it's used for.
pairs: Separating an insoluble solid from a liquid
Getting a soluble solid out of a solution
Getting a solvent out of a solution
Separating dissolved substances, like the dyes in ink
questions.explanation: Mixtures can be separated by physical processes because the substances in them aren't chemically joined.

questions.prompt: What is a compound?
questions.correct: Two or more elements chemically combined in fixed proportions
wrong: Two or more elements mixed but not chemically combined
A substance made of only one type of atom
Any substance that is a liquid
questions.explanation: A compound has two or more elements chemically combined in fixed proportions; it can only be separated by chemical reactions.

questions.prompt: Why did Mendeleev leave gaps in his periodic table?
questions.correct: For elements he predicted existed but hadn't been discovered yet
wrong: Because he ran out of space
For the noble gases he had already found
questions.explanation: Mendeleev left gaps for undiscovered elements; when they were found, their properties matched his predictions.

questions.prompt: Where are metals found in the periodic table?
questions.correct: On the left and towards the bottom
wrong: On the right and towards the top
questions.explanation: Most elements are metals, found to the left and towards the bottom. Non-metals are to the right and top.

questions.prompt: Compared with the Group 1 metals, transition metals usually…
questions.correct: have higher melting points and are much less reactive
wrong: have lower melting points and are more reactive
questions.explanation: Transition metals have higher melting points (except mercury), are denser, stronger and harder, and much less reactive.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a typical property of transition metal compounds?
questions.explanation: Many transition metal compounds are coloured, and transition metals and their compounds are often useful catalysts.

questions.prompt: The relative charge of a neutron is ___.
questions.explanation: Neutrons have no charge (0); that's why they're called neutrons.

questions.prompt: Chlorine is 75% chlorine-35 and 25% chlorine-37. What is its relative atomic mass?
Roughly how big is the radius of an atom?
questions.explanation: Atoms have a radius of about 0.1 nm (1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m); the nucleus is less than 1/10 000 of that.
